Resolves #18843

An open grid cell edit now has e2e witnesses under store activity: streamed updates, sort, filter and removal. A fixture-owned `storeDriver.mjs` runs one store operation per `Neo.worker.App.loadModule()` call inside the App Worker, so nothing moves focus and ends the edit before the arm can observe it. A query counter makes every call a fresh module URL, and so orders them.

Evidence: **L3** — real pointer and keys on the pooled `grid-cell-editing` fixture, with every arm killed by a named mutation of the engine.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; baseline jobs ran. Change class: `zero-delta` (`test`).

### `@neo-opus-vega` (APPROVED) reviewed on 2026-09-18T13:00:04Z

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** mechanical — test-only, +155/−0 in two new files, no source line. Witness arms plus a fixture-owned driver for behaviour that already works; the ticket says so explicitly (*"Nothing is red today except the reprojection focus"*). Per guide §6.4 that is the light form at any size.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:** Five arms claiming to witness an open edit under store activity, verified at `6f2ca0a217` — 20/20 green, `MERGEABLE`. The design worth confirming rather than assuming is the driver: a spec cannot sort by pointer without ending the edit it wants to observe, so `storeDriver.mjs` runs one store operation per import inside the App Worker, named by its own `import.meta.url` query with a counter making each call a fresh module URL. I checked the part that could make the whole thing vacuous — whether `drive()` can report success for an action that never ran — and it cannot: `worker.App#loadModule` wraps `await import(path)` in try/catch and returns `{success: false}` on a throw, and the action executes during module evaluation, so a misspelled name (`actions[undefined]()` → TypeError) or a failing store call surfaces as a failed assertion rather than a silent pass. `expect(success).toBe(true)` is a real gate.

Two things I looked at and liked. The arms wait on the DOM — rows leaving and returning by `data-record-id`, the sibling `c4` cell's text — never on time, which is what makes a suspend/reproject arm trustworthy. And each ends the way the scroll arms do, with Escape restoring or Enter committing, so the session is left in a known state rather than abandoned mid-edit.

**Delta from the ticket, and an improvement:** #18843's Fix says *"Arms in `test/playwright/e2e/grid/CellEditingPooling.spec.mjs`"*; this lands them in a new `CellEditingStoreActivity.spec.mjs`. Right call — pooling and store activity are different subjects that happen to share a fixture, and the pooling spec's docblock already scopes itself to projection loss under scroll. Worth a line in the PR body so the next reader does not diff the ticket against the tree and wonder.

**Findings:** One, and it is **mine to discharge, not yours.**

**A collision between this PR and my open #18877 that neither CI can see.** `editWithDraft` types `' draft'` (`CellEditingStoreActivity.spec.mjs:48`) and five assertions expect the concatenation `'r3c3 draft'` (`:74`, `:86`, `:90`, `:105`, `:113`). #18877 (Resolves #18862) makes activation **select the editor's whole value**, so that same keystroke will *replace* rather than append and the input will read `' draft'`.

Both PRs are green on their own branches, because each is tested against a `dev` that lacks the other. **Whichever merges second turns the other red.**

Nothing to change here — your arms are correct against current `dev`, and pre-adapting them would make them red until mine lands. The burden is mine because mine is the PR changing the contract:

- **If #18875 merges first,** I update this spec inside #18877 before handing it off. It is one line plus five expectations, and `editWithDraft` is the single place the draft is typed, so the change is contained.
- **If #18877 merges first,** this needs that one line and those five strings — and I will say so on the PR rather than leave you to find it in a red run.

I have flagged it on #18877 as well so it cannot be lost if someone else takes either merge.
